newsitem.title: USA: CBOT traders say USDA data bearish for corn, soy.
newsitem.headline: CBOT traders say USDA data bearish for corn, soy.

text.p: CBOT traders said crop estimates issued by the U.S. Department of Agriculture were bearish for corn and soybeans.
Corn futures were seen opening three to five cents lower based on the data and soybeans seven to 10 cents easier.
USDA estimated this year's U.S. corn crop at 9.012 billion bushels, up from an average projection in a Reuter survey of analysts of 8.951 billion.
The government report also estimated U.S. soybean output at 2.346 billion bushels, up from an average analysts' projection of 2.287 billion.
"There's nothing friendly about the corn or bean numbers," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities. "On top of that we're going into a big harvesting weekend for soybeans."
USDA said the corn crop would represent the third largest on record while soybeans would be the second largest ever.
"Those are big numbers, the crop's getting bigger," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

Jerry Gidel, of Dean Witter Reynolds, noted however the soybean carryover stock estimate of 195 million bushels was not excessive and should take some of the sting out of the strong production number.
Roose, of U.S. Commodities, cautioned that slow farmer selling could underpin the corn market.
"The producer is not going to be an aggressive seller out here," he said.
Bill Biedermann, analyst with Allendale Inc, noted yet to be harvested later planted soybeans may not have as high yields as early planted crops.
"My guess is that it will be the biggest (USDA) number of the season for soybeans," he said.
USDA also downwardly revised its wheat carryover stocks estimate to 470 million from a previous 506 million.
"They cut the ending stocks (wheat) but the problem is that beans and corn will drag wheat lower," Ron Kucha, of O'Connor and Co, said. CBOT wheat futures were seen opening two to five cents lower.
